Chili’s face is readable and clear of the mud. The visible crowd laughs, points and reacts from safe rails. No main cast is teleported in as spectators. A dropped hat at arm’s reach, readable outlaw belt and the expansive empty space between Chili and the gate make the humiliation personal. The shot retains enough of the stands to prove it happened in front of everyone.

DK casts around Chili’s upper arms/torso, never the neck; the rope catch and slipping boot precede the fall. Both stop; DK manually secures the hogtie with visible handwork. No instant knot. Hat falls during the caught turn and lies beside Chili in the payoff; his face remains visible above mud.

draft_copy.headline: One More Bag
draft_copy.deck: Red Leopards vs El Niño
draft_copy.body: Red Leopards pressed another sandbag against the pitch’s low edge. Water slid through the old wheel ruts and gathered beneath the wrecked goal. He moved a bag, then another. The river rose gently enough to make each small success feel useful, and steadily enough to take it away. Beyond the banners, El Niño’s front kept coming.

Develop this Retained Pass2 staging, reviewed in Pass3 as ONE cohesive full-page 1080 × 1920 cinematic PNG. Compose the action, environment, title, narration and any source-authorized factual lettering together.

Existing anchor and proposed local set: Trade Jedi Mountain Base; Ridge Gate. Durable proposed landmarks: worn inner arch coping with one visible repaired joint sheltered fixed lantern ridge shelf below existing war-room overlook Event dressing: two temporary attacking batteries initially LLC command position Movement: Main approach and elevated shelf converge toward LLC; the inner arch remains the defended return point.

Decisive moment: Obi uses the terrain for an aggressive second attempt; surviving fire blocks his route. Camera: Side view from the same side of the approach, raised enough to reveal the shelf without reversing screen direction. Foreground: Blackened first emplacement and wind-driven smoke below. Midground: Obi committed along the upper route. Background: LLC and the sole remaining battery across the approach.

Local lighting: Wreck is now an established warm source; smoke and cloak agree on wind. Ambient: Cool exposed upland light dimmed by the front. Fixed sources: warm sheltered gate lantern burning first battery after beat one Moving sources: green blade red volleys Storm relation: Crosswind aligns cloak, smoke and loose cloth; lightning is occasional background illumination, not every-page spectacle.

Shared storm, local expression: Low cloud masks the distant ridge without hiding the action plane. A recurring wind direction pulls robes, suit coat edges, smoke and small debris consistently. Cold damp stone and occasional driven droplets reflect weapon light. Obi uses a familiar sheltered recess before taking the exposed ridge route. Weather changes visibility and footing, but the two counterattacks and LLC firepower decide the scene. Ambient: Blue-grey cloud-filtered late-day sky with readable stone texture. Fixed practicals: Warm gate lantern behind shelter Orange fire from the first destroyed battery once established Moving sources: Green blade Red firing from the surviving battery and troops Continuity: The same gust carries the wreck smoke in the same world direction. A lightning flash can punctuate one beat; it must not become the permanent key light.

Lived-in set: The footpath has a polished walking line and rougher edges, suggesting repeated supply trips. One repair uses a slightly different stone; its age and cause are not invented. Gate hardware and tied-back working cloth imply routine use before the attack.

Character and costume continuity: Obi stays youthful/blond with earth-toned working layers, green blade and separate golden retriever; no belt. LLC keeps suit, red tie and sunglasses; a gust may lift a jacket edge, but no Vader-mask replacement. Wear on hems and fastenings belongs to use; fresh scorch and wetness enter only after the action.

Checks: Two initial batteries, one surviving. Retriever stays protected and separate. Weather complicates the action but LLC’s pressure remains the competitive mechanism. Current selected copy and all numeric lettering stay bound to the companion page contract. Retained detailed staging and final sports branch remain under review; do not treat this brief as artwork approval.

draft_copy.headline: Unlimited Firepower
draft_copy.deck: ObiWan Jacoby vs The LLC
draft_copy.body: The second counterattack vanished beneath converging red fire. reversal.title: The Green Line Breaks Through
reversal.copy: ObiWan Jacoby used the first battery’s wreckage to draw the crossfire, then changed direction beneath the stone arch. His second assault reached the command platform before the surviving guns could turn. The LLC stepped back as the green blade cut through the firing controls. Across the causeway, the advancing formation stopped receiving its orders, and the Jedi kept moving.

unresolved.title: The Encounter Remains Open
unresolved.copy: Red fire crossed the causeway while ObiWan Jacoby held his green blade toward the command platform. One battery burned behind him; the second counterattack had reached the ridge but not the commander. The LLC lifted a hand toward the surviving guns. Between those two movements, the entire mountain approach remained an unfinished blaze.

tie.title: Neither Side Gives
tie.copy: The last battery fell silent as ObiWan Jacoby reached the broken edge of the command approach. The LLC held the far platform, and the green blade held the inner arch, with neither able to cross the smoking gap. Both counterattacks had been spent. Both lines still stood. The mountain carried the marks of a battle neither side could finish.
